narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and your requested installment rate as a percentage of income. Your credit history of having all prior loans paid back at this bank was the single biggest driver pushing the prediction toward bad credit risk. Although it sounds positive, in this dataset that specific history is quite rare among approved applicants and the model treats it as a warning sign rather than a strength. The status of your checking account, which is currently in negative balance, was the second strongest factor and also pulled the decision toward denial; only 12.6% of approved customers show a negative balance, so this placed you in a higher-risk group. 

On a more positive note, the low installment rate you requested (1% of your disposable income versus the 3% average among approved loans) worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. Unfortunately, these two negative factors outweighed the benefit of the lower payment burden.

You should focus on improving your checking-account balance and building a more typical positive credit history with this bank. Once those areas look stronger, reapply and you are likely to receive a more favorable decision. (218 words)
